findings.produced: Two parallel hand-rolled fence-stripping helpers: strip_markdown_fences (coordinator.rs:197) and strip_json_fences (rerank.rs:153)
findings.rationale: Not strictly a severed wire — the canonical parser is wired to splitting.rs and the helpers chose simpler heuristic (zero-borrow &str → &str). But these are parallel implementations of a concern the canonical parser already covers; they diverge on indented fences, tilde fences, 4+ backtick fences, whitespace inside info strings, multiple concatenated fences, and case-sensitivity of the JSON tag. In practice LLM output is overwhelmingly ```json{...}```, so the divergence has not produced observed bugs.
findings.proposed_change: Either (1) keep as-is (recommended — ergonomic, no current pain), or (2) add fences::strip_outer_json_fence(text: &str) -> Option<&str> as a thin wrapper around parse_fence_spans and have both helpers delegate to it. Single source of truth, zero-borrow preserved, tighter parsing.
findings.risk: Option 2 changes behavior of both helpers in edge cases — strictly tightening, but the unclosed-fence / multi-anchored-fence handling now treats the input as 'extending to EOF' rather than 'strip what you can'. Whether LLM-output callers want that tighter behavior is a product call. New helper would need additional test cases mirroring the divergences above.
